events.excerpt: On October 19, 2026, we learned about eMudhra’s eight shockingly weak keys: where eMudhra was trusted to pick a 115-digit number for their virtual combination lock protecting the Internet, they picked the number 4. Not even four digits, just the number 4. The other seven keys were similarly weak: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. The next day, we wrote a blog post on the immediate action we took to mitigate this leak, and what customers needed to do on their end to stay secure. Now, we are sharing a more in-depth follow up on the evidence we’ve seen of exploitation, and the progress seen on visitors patching their systems. Let's start with the scale of the problem. A certificate authority (CA) with weak keys this serious is unprecedented, and the potential consequences are significant. While there have been plenty of compromised certification authorities in the past (such as DigiNotar , TÜRKTRUST , and TrustWave ), access to their keys has always been contained to a degree; these incidents gave a limited set of attackers or organizations the ability to issue fraudulent certificates. The eMudhra incident is fundamentally different; the affected intermediate private keys could be recovered almost instantly by anyone from the public certificates themselves. Anyone can independentl

The first pool is live for our Wish for Change #676 . We are asking for code review and people to try the Paseo rehearsal. This is experimental and has not had an independent review. We deployed before that review to leave time before #676 times out. A killed referendum loses the deposit, and a contract bug could also put contributions at risk. Kusama pool : real KSM. Paseo rehearsal : free test PAS. Source, tests and logs . Verified Kusama contract . How it works Each pool is fixed to one referendum and its exact deposit. If placement fails, the contribution stays in the pool and anyone can retry. Contributors can withdraw while the pool remains open, before placement. events.excerpt: Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection . Your origin stays private, while web application firewall ( WAF ), caching , bot management , and Workers work just as they do for public origins. In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet. Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin. Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers. What is generally available today During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group. I am not affiliated with Cosmos Labs, the Interchain Foundation, or the Cosmos Hub development team. This is not an official initiative or a finalized technical specification. My intention is to share an idea and gather community feedback. TL;DR I would like to propose exploring ATOM Shield , a limited emergency freezing mechanism for native ATOM on the Cosmos Hub. The goal is to prevent stolen ATOM from being moved further during major security incidents, without halting the entire network, while leaving final decisions to decentralized governance. The proposed mechanism would work as follows: 1 Security Council member: Initiates an immediate freeze lasting up to 1 hour. Additional Council approval: Extends the freeze for up to 24 hours from the initial action. At least 2/3 of all active Council members within 24 hours: Confirms the freeze until governance reaches a decision. Cosmos Hub governance: Decides whether to unfreeze, maintain the freeze, or authorize recovery of the assets. Failure to meet approval thresholds: Results in automatic unfreezing. events.excerpt: Digital signatures control who can spend funds, issue commands and authorize requests. Widely used schemes rely on factoring or discrete logarithms, assumptions threatened by Shor’s quantum algorithm. The post-quantum transition therefore reaches the mechanism used to establish authority itself. Post-quantum signatures provide replacements with different security assumptions, key sizes, signature sizes and verification costs. Applications that also prove execution must express that verification in their proof arithmetic. Signatureless authorization takes a direct proof-of-knowledge approach. An authority publishes a commitment to a reusable secret. Each action is authorized by a freshly randomized zero-knowledge proof of knowledge of that secret, bound to the requested action. The central security problem is safe reuse: an adversary can collect valid proofs, adapt later requests to earlier responses and attempt to authorize a fresh request. The linked paper develops this construction and proves a quantum chosen-request security reduction in an explicit address-compatible random-completion model. It also establishes the bindings for recursive verification. Parano1d supplies the implementation and measurements. The interface supports both standalone requests and authorization compo
events.headline: Post-quantum signatureless authorization with recursive verification

Highest synergy because they compose cleanly with independent simulation (the simulation result can be bound into the capability) and with account authority lifecycle (capabilities are issued, used, and revoked under explicit lifecycle rules). events.excerpt: At 8:08am HKT, 30th October 2026, the Security Council executed an emergency action to freeze 8,425 ETH and 74,559,805.2 ARB held on Arbitrum One by an address identified with today’s Binance exploit. The funds are now held at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000DA0 . The funds can only be moved by an ArbitrumDAO Governance vote, which will be coordinated with relevant parties. Key point: Funds associated with the Binance exploit are frozen on Arbitrum One. No other user’s funds or applications were affected. Security Council Actions The technical approach taken by the Security Council was to implement an atomic action to upgrade the inbox contract on Ethereum, freeze the funds, and return the contract back to its original implementation. The Inbox Contract was upgraded to add a new function, sendUnsignedTransactionOverride , which imitates the structure of a standard cross-chain transaction with the ability to impersonate the transaction sender. Two cross-chain transactions were created to impersonate the address associated with the Binance exploit, and these transactions transferred the stolen funds to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000DA0 . events.excerpt: Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report. This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 — July, August, and September — and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume. The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One , Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network . Key insights Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%. Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year. However, variants continue to emerge, proving that IoT botnets remain a durable, high-volume threat to network infrastructure. Threat actors dramatically shifted their reflection and amplification tactics, abruptly abandoning CLDAP floods, which collapsed by 99.5% quarter-over-quarter. Instead, attackers pivoted heavily toward other connectionless protocols, driving a 215% surge in DNS amplification and a 122% increase in general UDP floods. Sky Governance maintains full control over cBEAM actions through Executive Votes or Core Council actions . events.excerpt: Strategy investors face a November 11 decision on whether the Bitcoin treasury company will remain in MSCI’s global equity indexes. Any resulting removals would take effect after the November 30 close. MSCI adopted its new eligibility rules on October 15. Strategy’s removal has not been confirmed; the issue for shareholders is how exclusion could affect demand for its shares and future financing. Separately, Strategy said on October 28 that shareholders had approved amendments permitting daily dividends on four preferred-stock series, based on preliminary voting results. Subject to the amended terms being filed and becoming effective, the new schedule would begin November 1 for STRC and January 1, 2027, for STRF, STRK and STRD. The vote changes preferred-dividend arrangements; it does not settle the MSCI index decision. $MSTR shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor. The amendment enables $STRF , $STRC , $STRK and $STRD to accrue dividends every calendar day. Thank you to all who voted. https://t.co/vRSC6hwlro — Strategy (@Strategy) October 28, 2026 How the new MSCI rules work MSCI first assesses whether a company has substantial operating assets . Companies that fail this screen face five financial-ratio
events.headline: Strategy’s MSCI risk: What to watch before November 11

The £22 billion figure describes the entire underlying fund; Aviva invested £50 million in the new share class. Big news as Aviva Investors announces the launch of a tokenized share class of the Aviva Investors Sterling (GBP) Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger. The Sterling (GBP) Liquidity Fund is Aviva Investors’ largest fund at around £22 billion in assets under management, and this move… — Ripple (@Ripple) October 26, 2026 The launch sits alongside a broader expansion of institutional blockchain services. events.excerpt: You can’t expect ATOM’s price to rise significantly while inflation continues to dilute holders and new tokens keep entering the market. Lower inflation. Fewer new tokens. A well-designed burn mechanism. Stronger real demand. These are the changes Cosmos needs to restore confidence in ATOM. Technical upgrades are important, but if they don’t translate into real demand for ATOM, what is the point? Holding ATOM must become genuinely attractive. The token needs stronger utility, and the growth of the Cosmos ecosystem must finally translate into value for ATOM holders. Cosmos has the potential, but potential alone is not enough. We need concrete decisions and measurable results. Without meaningful tokenomics reform and sustainable demand, ATOM risks continuing to underperform, even if the ecosystem keeps growing. It’s time to stop making promises and start delivering results. ATOM deserves better. 5 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
events.headline: ATOM needs a tokenomics overhaul, and it needs it now

events.excerpt: A standard interface and workflow for verifiable, human-readable transaction simulation, scoped authorization, and independent verification of signing payloads for EOAs, smart accounts, and multisigs. author: @MATOBOYCRYPTO65 discussions-to: (ERC Draft), Secure Transaction Verification and Authorization (STVA) – Stopping Blind Signing & Multisig UI Attacks - ERCs - Fellowship of Ethereum Magicians status: Draft type: Standards Track category: ERC created: 2026-10-27 Abstract: This ERC defines a standard for Secure Transaction Verification and Authorization (STVA) It provides: 1. A canonical way to attach structured, human-readable metadata and semantic intent to any transaction or UserOperation. 2. A mandatory independent simulation and verification interface that wallets, signers, and verifiers can call. 3. Scoped, revocable capability tokens attestations for privileged operations (upgrades, large transfers, module installation, ownership changes). 4. Clear requirements for multisig and smart-account signing ceremonies that resist frontend supply-chain attacks and UI spoofing. events.excerpt: Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we’ve gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters. Today at GitHub Universe , we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it. Our vision: From idea to completed software The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Agents implement and verify changes. And everything feeds into and out of a continuous learning machine that makes the next cycle better. This agentic software delivery system solves for three things: Velocity: get from idea to completed software as quickly, efficiently, and cost-effectively as possible Intelligence: comb
events.headline: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack

events.excerpt: Developers pushed code to GitHub 17.9 billion times in the past 12 months, more than in 2024 and 2025 combined. Behind that number are developers building what interests them and what their communities need. In Nepal, one developer built a flood bulletin on GitHub Pages with verified information on roads, rescue, weather, and power. It has since grown into Gati , a Nepali-first relay of official disaster alerts that runs on GitHub Pages and Actions. Elsewhere, developers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are creating software designed to run programs aboard spacecraft , and fans built open-source firmware that lets people customize their e-readers . Curiosity, aimed in every direction, at a scale GitHub hasn’t seen before. That growth happened quickly. Partway through the year, activity on GitHub bent sharply upward, just as agents went from something developers were trying out to something they were working alongside. Developers picked from more models than ever and built in industries we are highlighting in this report for the first time, from health care to agriculture. Octoverse is our chance to step back and look at the whole picture. This year, that picture is bigger than ever. Here is what stood out most: More AI, more of everything. Among repositories created this year,
events.headline: Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents

events.excerpt: Protocol This release introduces protocol version 39 On testnet , this protocol version can be enabled no earlier than 2026-10-28 19:23 UTC (start of epoch 710). Please ensure that you update your validators before this epoch change. Otherwise, if the upgrade threshold is reached, the protocol will remove you from the committee, and both you and your delegators will lose rewards. #13131 : From protocol version 39 on devnet and testnet, random beacon DKG that misses its timeout round keeps running and can enable randomness again mid-epoch instead of disabling it for the rest of the epoch. #13169 : Protocol version 39 enables consensus_dedup_only_recorded_messages on all chains. A consensus message is skipped as a duplicate only of an earlier message with the same key that was recorded as processed or, in the same commit, passed verification, so all validators reach the same decision about a later copy of a dropped message. #13300 : Raise the minimum validator joining stake to 6M IOTA, the low stake threshold to 5.5M IOTA and the very low stake threshold to 5M IOTA. #13285 : From protocol version 39, a multisig whose committee mixes Ed25519 with other key schemes is only accepted when every committee member has signed. #13308 : groth16::prepare_verifying_key and groth16::verify_gro
